title: Civil dispute: neighbour parked across driveway

caller.name: Gerald Foster
caller.persona: indignant, pompous, convinced this is a police matter, prone to speeches
caller.openingLine: Yes, hello, I want to report a crime. My neighbour has deliberately parked his caravan across the end of my driveway AGAIN and I am completely blocked in. I pay my road tax. I want him arrested, or at the very least a stern word.

incident.summaryTruth: Gerald Foster, 22 Beech Grove, Haywards Heath, reports his neighbour Keith's caravan parked across his dropped kerb, blocking his car in. Ongoing feud between the two over parking for years. No threats, no damage, no breach of the peace, neighbour is not even home. Obstruction of a dropped kerb is a council parking matter; the dispute itself is civil. No policing purpose. Correct handling: explain, refer to the council and to legal advice, log and close.

facts.label: Caller's name
facts.beat: Gerald Foster. That's F-O-S-T-E-R, and I'd like a reference number for this call.

facts.label: Address
facts.beat: 22 Beech Grove, Haywards Heath. RH16 3PQ. The caravan in question is directly across my dropped kerb.

facts.label: What has actually happened
facts.value: caravan parked across his dropped kerb
facts.beat: What's happened is Keith's enormous caravan is parked bang across the end of my drive. My Jaguar is imprisoned. I have a golf tee time at half past four.

facts.label: Threats or violence
facts.beat: Threats? No, no. He's not even in, that's the point. His curtains are shut and the caravan sits there mocking me.

facts.label: Damage
facts.beat: No damage as such, no. It's the principle. And the tee time.

facts.label: History of the dispute
facts.value: years-long parking feud with neighbour Keith
facts.beat: Ohh, this has been going on for years. Keith and I have history. The wheelie bin incident of 2023, the leylandii, I could go on. It's all documented in my ledger.
